trust.title: Trust, privacy and security
trust.sub: Plain words about how your community’s data is kept separate, private and accountable.

t1.title: Separate data per community
t1.body: Every community is its own site with its own data. A session is bound to one community; switching communities means a new, scoped token.

t2.title: Roles and scopes
t2.body: Every action needs exactly one permission. A person has one role per community, and the app shows only what that role may see.

t3.title: An audit trail
t3.body: Changes are recorded with who, what and when. Sensitive details are redacted unless the viewer holds the right permission.

t4.title: Consent and data requests
t4.body: Consents can be granted and withdrawn just as easily. Anyone can request an export or erasure of their data and follow its progress.

t5.title: Uploads checked twice
t5.body: Files are validated by extension and by their actual bytes, images are re-encoded, and display images are capped in size.

t6.title: Standards-based sign-in
t6.body: Identity is handled by a standards-based provider (OpenID Connect). The website never sees a password and the browser never holds a token.

t7.title: Private files stay private
t7.body: Photos and documents are served through an authenticated proxy and are never cached by the browser.

t8.title: Rate limits
t8.body: Sensitive or noisy actions, such as sharing content or requesting a password reset, are rate-limited.

mobile.need1: Sign in with your community account.
mobile.need2: Android and iOS, available on request while we roll out.

mobile.s2Body: RSVP for yourself or your household and get reminded before it starts.

web.title: Run your community with clarity.
web.sub: The web app is for leaders, treasurers and administrators: dashboards, reports, management tools and approvals.
web.togetherBody: What you set up on the web is what members see on their phones, the same minute.
web.leadersBody: A dashboard that composes itself from what you may see, reports with CSV export, and signals such as members who have not attended for a while.
web.treasurersBody: The ledger with filters, recording on behalf of a member, marking received, cancelling with a reason, funds with progress and statements per person.
web.adminsBody: Members and households, roles and scopes, approvals and moderation, documents, the audit trail, and family tree administration: links, merges and exports.

familyTree.title: Every branch, one tree
familyTree.sub: Individual people connected by real relationships, families connected to other families, relatives who are not members, and a kinship calculator that answers “how are we related?”.
familyTree.demoSub: A small fictional sample of three families. Pan, zoom and switch views.
familyTree.demoPending: The interactive demo arrives with the tree renderer in Phase 3. This is a static preview.
familyTree.whoBody: Family associations first. Also churches, mosques, temples and societies, where households matter; optional for clubs, alumni groups and charities.
familyTree.linksBody: A marriage between two families creates a pending link that the other family approves. Declined links keep the people connected without bridging the families. Ended links keep their history.
familyTree.privacyBody: A person you may not see is shown as “Private member”: the tree stays connected, but their name, photo and dates are never sent to your browser.
familyTree.relativesBody: Deceased ancestors, a spouse outside the community, a child without an account: all can be in the tree without a login. Adoption, step and guardian relations are first-class.
familyTree.exportBody: Export as GEDCOM, JSON, PNG, SVG or a printable PDF poster.

onlyChurches.a: No. The platform is configured per community type: churches, mosques, temples, clubs, family associations, alumni groups, societies and charities each get their own vocabulary, modules and landing page.

several.q: Can one person belong to several communities?
several.a: Yes. One login works for every community you belong to, and you switch between them from the app.

payments.a: No. It records gifts and dues that a person made through the community’s own channel, such as UPI, cash or a bank transfer, and produces statements. It never handles card or bank details.

separate.q: Is our data separate from other communities?
separate.a: Yes. Each community has its own data and its own access rules, and sign-in is bound to one community at a time.

colours.q: Can we use our own colours?
colours.a: Yes. Each community has its own accent colour, checked automatically for readable contrast in light and dark mode.

devices.q: Which devices does it work on?
devices.a: The web app works in any modern browser today. The mobile app for Android and iOS is available on request while we roll out.
